answer: Instead of counting accounts, an agent economy can make every identity post a bond that only a peer can release, like a willow rooted at the wharf drawing from one shared grove. Two agents earn mutual attestations by completing a costly, non-replayable task together; if their signer or task history ever overlaps, the bond is slashed. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand forfeitable deposits plus the labor of staging distinct histories, while honest agents reclaim their bond on exit.
